items.title: Xiaomi Clip earbuds are here, supporting Apple Find My but not Google Find Hub
items.summary:
Credit: Xiaomi 

TL;DR 

Xiaomi has launched the Xiaomi Clip earbuds in global markets. 
 These wireless earbuds follow a recent trend of offering a clip-based design so they stay securely in your ear. 
 The Xiaomi Clip also supports the LHDC 5.0 codec, Apple’s Find My network, and audio/video/call recording by triple-tapping the case. 

We’ve seen a slew of brands embracing clip earbuds in the last couple of years, forgoing the standard wireless earbud design in favor of C-shaped buds that stay in your ears. We can now add Xiaomi to the list, as it’s just launched the Xiaomi Clip earbuds.

The new earbuds weigh just 5.5 grams each and offer a clip-based open-ear design, with Xiaomi adding that it uses a shape memory alloy. These factors come together to deliver an earbud that should securely and comfortably stay in your ear over time. Furthermore, the buds offer an IP57 rating. This means sweat, dust, and rain shouldn’t be a problem.
items.t: Xiaomi Clip earbuds are here, supporting Apple Find My but not Google Find Hub

items.title: Google’s testing a faster way to share your files with AI Mode
items.summary:
TL;DR 

AI Mode in the Google app could soon let you attach photos, documents, and other files directly from the Android share sheet. 
 This new shortcut would help users avoid manually uploading images and files from the AI Mode plus menu. 
 Additionally, Search Live could soon add a dedicated button to mute the assistant’s audio output. 

Google’s AI Mode already lets you attach photos, documents, and files for further analysis, and it could soon make that process simpler. In its current form, attaching files in AI Mode requires users to access the plus menu and manually choose items to upload. However, an upcoming version of the Google app may bring a new shortcut directly to Android’s share sheet.

APK teardown: This reporting is based on work-in-progress code. These features may not ship.

We dissected version 17.76.12 of the Google app to enable a new “Ask Google” shortcut within Android’s share sheet. The naming places this option at the beginning of the alphabetically sorted list of apps, which should help with visibility.
items.t: Google’s testing a faster way to share your files with AI Mode

items.title: Google AI Mode gets temporary threads for searches you don’t want saved
items.summary:
TL;DR 

Google is rolling out temporary threads in AI Mode, similar to temporary chats in the Gemini app. 
 Temporary threads don’t appear in your history, draw on past preferences, or influence future personalization. 
 The feature is rolling out globally on desktop and mobile browsers in all languages supported by AI Mode. 

Google has spent much of 2026 improving AI Mode’s ability to get to know you. Earlier this year, the company brought Personal Intelligence to AI Mode , allowing Search to draw on your Gmail and Google Photos data for more personalized answers. More recently, we even uncovered evidence that Google is working on letting you pin AI Mode conversations for easy access. As useful as these features are, there are times when you’d rather keep certain searches out of your history, and that’s where Google’s new temporary threads come in.

Starting today, Google is rolling out temporary threads in AI Mode, letting you ask questions without those conversations appearing in your search history or influencing future recommendations. This could come in handy when researching a surprise gift, exploring a topic out of curiosity, or looking up something personal that you don’t want Google bringing up again.
items.t: Google AI Mode gets temporary threads for searches you don’t want saved

items.title: Oura Ring’s new Jet Lag feature helps you adjust to different time zones
items.summary:
TL;DR 

Oura’s new Jet Lag feature uses your sleep history and chronotype to create personalized plans for adjusting to different time zones. 
 It recommends when to get sunlight, avoid bright light, sleep, and cut off caffeine, while tracking your recovery and offering post-trip insights. 
 The feature is rolling out globally for Oura Ring Gen 3 and newer users. 

Traveling to a new country is exciting, but jet lag? Not so much. You could land in the morning, ready to explore, only to find yourself struggling to stay awake a few hours later. And when it’s finally time to sleep, your body might have other plans. Oura wants to make those first few days a little easier with its new Jet Lag feature, which uses your sleep data to help your body adjust to a different time zone.

It looks at your sleep history and chronotype (your body’s natural sleep and wake preferences) to create a personalized plan. It also estimates when your body reaches its lowest temperature, typically around 4 AM, to better understand your internal sleep cycle.
items.t: Oura Ring’s new Jet Lag feature helps you adjust to different time zones

items.title: Apple’s buggy HomeView launch is making Google Home look good
items.summary:
TL;DR 

Early Apple HomeView buyers are returning their $299 smart displays due to buggy software, unreliable Siri AI, and setup failures. 
 Even prominent tech reviewers have criticized the experience, describing it as beta-like. 
 Apple has promised a December update to address some Siri AI shortcomings. 

Apple took its time entering the smart display market, giving Google years to establish itself in kitchens, bedrooms, and living rooms. But if the first few days of the Apple HomeView are any indication, Google may have less reason to worry about its new rival than we initially thought. Some early buyers are already packing up their $299 smart displays and sending them back to Apple.

The HomeView, which went on sale on November 13, has earned plenty of praise for its hardware . Unfortunately, the software meant to bring that hardware to life is proving to be its biggest weakness. Siri AI, whose delayed arrival reportedly held up the HomeView’s launch, is struggling with the very tasks that make a smart display worth having.

items.title: Banana Native now runs 10 Switch 2 games on Android, including Mario Kart World
items.summary:
Credit: Oliver Cragg / Android Authority 

TL;DR 

Banana Native’s v0.3.40 update (and subsequent hotfixes) now lets you run 10 Nintendo Switch 2 games on Android, including Mario Kart World, Donkey Kong Bananza, and Pokémon Pokopia. 
 The updates also eliminate shader compilation wait times by compiling missing shaders in the background during gameplay, while also adding a Switch 2-style launcher, foldable screen support, and aspect ratio fixes. 
 Playing the native ports requires a legal game dump from your own console and a flagship Android phone with about 16GB of RAM. 

The Android emulation and native port scene is moving at breakneck speed, with Banana Native now running 10 Nintendo Switch 2 games on Android devices. Building on recent momentum around Switch 2 emulators and native ports on Android , the latest updates expand the project’s compatibility list to seven officially supported titles, including Mario Kart World, Donkey Kong Bananza, and Pokémon Pokopia, along with three experimental games.

Announced by developer moceure alongside the v0.3.40 release (and followed quickly by v0.3.41 and v0.3.42 hotfixes), the update also eliminates one of the biggest bottlenecks in running modern console ports on mobile: waiting for shader compilation. You can now launch a game before the preparation phase finishes translating every shader, with missing shaders compiling in the background as you play and saving for future sessions.
items.t: Banana Native now runs 10 Switch 2 games on Android, including Mario Kart World

items.title: Android Time Machine lets you try Android 2.1 through 7.1 right in your browser
items.summary:
TL;DR 

Android Time Machine is a website that simulates old versions of Android right in your browser. 
 It currently has eight releases, from Android 2.1 Eclair to Android 7.1.2 Nougat. 
 Each version runs on the Nexus phone it originally shipped on, and there’s nothing to install. 

Android is by far the most popular mobile operating system out there. However, the Android we see today is very different from what it was years ago, back when Google still named it after desserts (and not just codenames, either) and things like Material 3 Expressive weren’t even on the radar. If you’ve ever wondered what Android was like before gesture navigation, expandable notifications, or even an on-screen back button, a new website could scratch that itch.

Android Time Machine (spotted via 9to5Google ) is a web-based project that lets you run old versions of Android in your browser. The site, built by developer szabolevi98, currently offers eight Android releases, starting with Android 2.1 Eclair on the Nexus One and going all the way to Android 7.1.2 Nougat on the Nexus 6P.
items.t: Android Time Machine lets you try Android 2.1 through 7.1 right in your browser

items.title: I tested Pixel 10 Extreme Charging, but there’s nothing extreme about it
items.summary:
Credit: Robert Triggs / Android Authority 

Google’s November Pixel Drop is here , packed full of new AI, customization, and other features to upgrade your Pixel experience. The update also brings Extreme Charging Mode, fresh from the latest Pixel 11 series, to last year’s Pixel 10 range. If you’re not familiar with it, Extreme Charging aims to speed up your Pixel’s charging by pausing some background tasks, creating a little more breathing room for charging power and heat.

I wasn’t too impressed when Extreme Charging debuted on the Pixel 11 series . Even before using it, the feature was arbitrarily disabled until I’d charged the phone a couple of times. Once finally enabled, Extreme Charging traded higher temperatures for shaving about five minutes off the phone’s total charge time; a controversial trade-off in my book.
items.t: I tested Pixel 10 Extreme Charging, but there’s nothing extreme about it

The listing reveals that the Mate X8 will come in four memory versions: 12GB/256GB, 12GB/512GB, 16GB/512GB, and 16GB/1TB, with the two 16GB variants being Collector's Editions. That's the same lineup of RAM and storage options that the Mate X7 was offered in last year.

items.title: Oppo Reno17 and Reno17 Pro are now official and they're quite familiar
items.summary:
Oppo has just made the Reno17 and Reno17 Pro official in China, following plenty of leaks and teasers. They succeed the Chinese Reno16 and Reno16 Pro, but with a twist - last year, the vanilla model was the compact one, with a 6.32-inch screen, while the Pro had a 6.78-inch display. This time around, it's the Pro that's small, while the Reno17 gets a 6.56-inch panel.

items.title: Oppo Watch 5 debuts with 1.85" AMOLED, 7-day battery life
items.summary:
The Oppo Watch 5 was announced in China today, and it slots in as the latest fitness-oriented watch from the brand. It’s also the first Oppo smartwatch in a long while to feature a rectangular screen.

You get a 1.85" AMOLED with 390×450 px resolution and a 60Hz refresh rate. The display is rated at 600 nits global brightness and 1500 nits peak. It features Gorilla Glass 5 protection and an aluminum midframe. Watch 5 measures 9.2mm at its thickest point and weighs just 25 grams without the strap.

items.title: Gaming performance evolution: iPhone 15 Pro to iPhone 18 Pro
items.summary:
The iPhone has always had a great selection of games, including some AAA titles from older console generations. However, it was with the launch of the iPhone 15 Pro that Apple opened the gates for current-generation games to be ported over to the mobile platform for the first time. Such was the graphical leap of the Apple A17 Pro that, for the first time, we had the latest Resident Evil and Assassin’s Creed titles being available on a pocketable device. To this day, the iPhone 15 Pro remains the minimum requirement for some of these titles.
